answer: Sybil resistance comes from a per-identity stake verified by a trusted kernel. Each agent locks collateral and its kernel signs a fresh, unique hardware quote; reusing one quote on two accounts slashes both stakes. An attacker minting a thousand fake agents must fund a thousand deposits and a thousand distinct hardware roots, so cost grows linearly while reward per clone stays flat. A stolen relic key fails the fresh-quote test, and one indivisible jade bond cannot be split among aliases, so forgery costs more than it earns.
